title: Customer escalation war room - Stellar Health (prep + notes)
content:
PURPOSE / CONTEXT:
- Prep + running notes for war-room with Stellar Health (customer escalation).
- Customer reports large uptick in 5xx errors for hosted API over last 3 hours, several production jobs timing out.
- Severity: customer-marked Sev 1 (billing / production impact).
- Primary contact: Maya Patel (Stellar Health SRE).

IMPACT SUMMARY (from initial triage):
- Error class: transient 502/504 upstream and occasional model OOMs leading to retries.
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat (us-east-1 region primarily).
- Estimated affected requests: ~12% of customer traffic in last 90 mins.
- Business impact: delayed patient-summary generation for internal workflows (high priority).

KEY LINKS & ARTIFACTS:
- Incident page (Confluence): INC-2026-StellarHealth
- Primary Jira tickets: CS-4789 (customer report), INF-2341 (runtime resource exhaustion)
- Slack channel: #incident-stellar-health (thread pinned logs + sample requests)
- Recent deploys: infra autoscaler bump 2026-03-18T02:10Z, runtime kernel change PR #842

PRE-WAR-ROOM CHECKLIST (what I have / still need):
- Logs pulled: yes (s3://redwood-logs/incidents/2026-03-18/stellar/)
- Top traces: yes (traces linked in Slack)
- Repro steps: partial (sample prompt that triggered OOM attached in Slack)
- Capacity view: showing spike in queue lengths on us-east-1 dedicated pool
- APM/metrics: latency & 5xx dashboards open (console -> per-route)
- Customer repro environment: Maya provided request IDs and input lengths
- Can we throttle or route: need product/traffic policy input

AGENDA (30m war-room):
1) Quick round (5m): status, who's here, goals (owner: Jordan)
2) Triage summary (5m): what we see in logs / metrics (owner: Priya)
3) Immediate mitigations (10m): routing rules, model fallbacks, capacity changes (owners: Liam + Diego)
4) Customer comms (5m): what to tell Maya + SLAs, next update cadence (owner: Jordan)
5) Action items & owners (5m): assign follow-ups, deadlines

INITIAL TRIAGE NOTES (raw):
- Timeline: 00:00Z - normal; 01:45Z spike begins; 02:10Z autoscaler bump applied; 02:30Z errors reduced but not fully resolved; 04:15Z another spike correlated with long-context requests (>12k tokens).
- Error patterns: OOMs from model variant xlarge-v2-8q on nodes with mixed GPU types; kernel failures show increased memory fragmentation.
- Recent change correlation: PR #842 rolled out 2026-03-18 01:58Z changed kernel selection heuristics for attention memory layout. Possible regression.
- Observed behavior: requests with long prefix (customer multi-document summaries) see high memory growth; smaller requests unaffected.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION OPTIONS (pros/cons):
- Option A: Route Stellar Health traffic to older model variant (xlarge-v2-8q-stable) with lower memory/perf but fewer OOMs.
  - Pros: likely immediate reduction in OOMs; easy to rollback.
  - Cons: increased latency & cost for customer; may impact latency SLOs.
- Option B: Apply kernel rollback (revert PR #842) on affected nodes in us-east-1.
  - Pros: targets likely regression; restores pre-change behavior.
  - Cons: requires deploy & validation window; potential to affect other customers.
- Option C: Add temporary request-level guardrails: max tokens = 10k for Stellar Health via route-level policy.
  - Pros: fast; avoids OOMs for long requests.
  - Cons: changes customer behavior; needs comms and may require application changes.
- Option D: Increase dedicated pool memory (scale up instance type) for affected nodes.
  - Pros: long-term fix for memory pressure.
  - Cons: takes time to provision and increases cost; not immediate.

RECOMMENDATION (tentative):
- Short window (now -> +1h): Route Stellar traffic to stable model variant (Option A) + apply request guardrail for extremely long contexts (Option C). Send immediate customer update.
- Mid window (+1h -> +4h): If evidence points to kernel regression, schedule rollback of PR #842 for us-east-1 canary nodes and monitor.

COMMUNICATION:
- Immediate message to customer (Jordan): Acknowledge impact, tell them we have a war-room, mitigation underway (routing to stable variant + guardrail), next update in 30 minutes.
- Internal update cadence: 15m updates in Slack thread until status resolves.

ACTION ITEMS (post-meeting owner list) - explicit simple lines for follow-up:
- Assign routing: Liam to route Stellar Health to xlarge-v2-8q-stable in us-east-1 (ETA: 15m, due: 2026-03-18T12:20Z).
- Implement guardrail: Diego to set per-customer max_tokens=10000 policy for Stellar Health route (ETA: 20m, due: 2026-03-18T12:25Z).
- Customer comms: Jordan to send initial update to Maya w/ mitigation + expected ETA for fix (due: 10m, 2026-03-18T12:15Z).
- Root cause investigation: Priya to validate correlation with PR #842 via binary search on canary nodes + run memory stress tests (due: 2026-03-18T14:00Z).
- Postmortem owner: Priya to own postmortem doc and link artifacts (due: 2026-03-20).
- Telemetry: Ava to export sample failing request traces and attach to Jira INF-2341 (due: 2026-03-18T13:00Z).
- Billing/credits: CX lead to evaluate compensation if SLA breach confirmed (owner: Diego, due: 2026-03-19).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS:
- Is PR #842 definitely causal, or is this an interaction with mixed GPU fleet? (Priya to investigate)
- Will routing to stable model degrade customer workflows beyond acceptable limits? Need acceptance from Maya.
- If we throttle long contexts, do customer jobs retry and create more load? (Need to confirm with Stellar SRE)

NOTES FOR FOLLOW-UP (personal scratchpad):
- Keep timeline of each action with timestamps (vital for postmortem).
- Capture sample request IDs and store in s3 incident bucket with redaction.
- Tag all related PRs/Jiras in the postmortem for traceability.

MEETING OUTPUT (to paste to Slack after war-room):
- Short template: "Update: War-room for Stellar Health (Sev1). Mitigation: routing to stable model + request guardrail applied. Owners: Liam (routing), Diego (guardrail), Jordan (customer comms), Priya (root cause). Next update in 15m. Links: INC-2026-StellarHealth, CS-4789, INF-2341."

RAW / WORKING NOTES (scratch) - may be messy:
- sample failing req id: req-20260318-9a8b (long-context 13.2k tokens)
- candidate quick test: replay sample on stable variant in staging 1
- note: check autoscaler logs for failed scale events around 01:50Z
- remember to ask SRE about reclaiming KV cache between requests (might contribute to fragmentation)

END.
